# Track Encoder

Current release: 0.1.0a4 (alpha).

Track Encoder learns compact fixed-length embeddings of genomic signal
associated with researcher-selected genomic elements. The researcher supplies
all inputs (genomic elements, signal tracks, a split assignment, reference
FASTA). Preparation publishes each split as its own processed dataset (a train
dataset, a val dataset, and a test dataset); reconstruction training (CUDA)
fits the train dataset and selects its full checkpoint on the val dataset;
evaluation (CUDA or CPU) scores a full checkpoint on any compatible dataset,
typically the test dataset; embedding export and reconstruction of selected
element examples use the trained model. Training configurations are version 3
and may add an optional W&B tracking block (the wandb extra; credentials only
through wandb login or WANDB_API_KEY), which mirrors per-epoch metrics without
changing training results. Datasets, training configurations, and checkpoints
from earlier releases must be regenerated or migrated; see Outputs. This file
is a link map only; the pages below are the complete guidance.

## Docs

- [Overview](https://dignomor.github.io/xp-track-encoder-doc/)
- [Inputs](https://dignomor.github.io/xp-track-encoder-doc/inputs/)
- [Preparation](https://dignomor.github.io/xp-track-encoder-doc/preparation/)
- [Training](https://dignomor.github.io/xp-track-encoder-doc/training/): train and val datasets, run artifacts, optional W&B tracking (Slurm and offline use)
- [Evaluation](https://dignomor.github.io/xp-track-encoder-doc/evaluation/): the `evaluate` command, test metrics from a full checkpoint
- [Embedding](https://dignomor.github.io/xp-track-encoder-doc/embedding/)
- [Reconstruction](https://dignomor.github.io/xp-track-encoder-doc/reconstruction/): the `reconstruct` command, from a full checkpoint and a boolean mask
- [Outputs](https://dignomor.github.io/xp-track-encoder-doc/outputs/)

## Install

- [xp-track-encoder installation](https://github.com/haiyuan-yu-lab/xp-track-encoder)

No input data is bundled with the docs. Examples use fictional names with
clearly marked absolute-path placeholders.
